question: In which year was the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana launched?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2015**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY)** was launched on **15th July 2015** by the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE).
 
• The scheme aims to provide industry-relevant skill training to youth and **enhance employability** by offering certification in various vocational skills.
 
• PMKVY is part of the National Skill Development Mission, which focuses on **skilling, reskilling, and upskilling** India’s workforce.
 
• Under PMKVY, candidates receive monetary rewards and skill certificates upon successful completion of training and assessment.
 
• It targets the **short-term training** needs of unemployed youth, school/college dropouts, and individuals seeking skill development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Skill Development Initiatives in India**

 
 
• The National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC) was established in 2008 to promote private sector participation in skill development.
 
• India aims to train over 400 million individuals by 2022 under the Skill India Mission.
 
• Other key programs include **Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY)** and **National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS).**
 
 
 
• **PMKVY Training Components**
 
 
• **Short-Term Training (STT):** Offered to school/college dropouts and unemployed individuals, covering industry-relevant skills.
 
• **Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL):** Aims to certify individuals with existing skills through assessments.
 
• **Special Projects:** Focus on training in unique locations, sectors, or groups that fall outside STT or RPL.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of PMKVY**
 
 
• Monetary incentives provided to trainees for completing training and assessment.
 
• Skill training aligned with **National Skills Qualification Framework (NSQF).**
 
• Special focus on **women, differently-abled individuals, and marginalized communities.**
 
 
 
• **Global Context of Skill Development**
 
 
• Countries like Germany, Japan, and South Korea have robust apprenticeship models for skill enhancement.
 
• India’s PMKVY is aligned with similar global frameworks, emphasizing youth employability and industry needs.
